high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Signals Pertamax Fuel Price Will Decline
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa expressed optimism that Pertamina's non-subsidized fuel Pertamax will see a price reduction as global oil prices continue to ease. Global oil prices have fallen significantly from above $100/barrel during the US-Israel-Iran conflict, with Brent now trading at $72.08 and WTI at $68.89 per barrel. A Pertamax price cut would help reduce inflationary pressures in Indonesia over the coming months, which is significant for consumers and monetary policy outlook.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Questioned Over Careless State Budget Spending, Vows Internal Review Team
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa acknowledged criticism over careless state budget expenditures, including the controversial purchase of electric motorcycles under the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program. In response, he has instructed the newly appointed Director General of the Budget, Sudarto, to form an internal team to scrutinize all budget proposals and prevent similar wasteful spending from slipping through. This signals a push for tighter fiscal discipline and budget oversight within the Ministry of Finance, with implications for government spending efficiency.

high.title: Indonesia to Roll Out Red Carpet for Foreign Investors Through International Financial Center (PFII)
high.summary: The Indonesian government is establishing the Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII), with the draft law currently being deliberated between the government and parliament, targeting completion before July 22, 2026. The PFII aims to attract foreign investment by offering special incentives including tax exemptions, tailored financial sector supervision, and streamlined company registration mechanisms. This represents a significant structural reform to position Indonesia as a competitive regional financial hub.

high.title: Tokopedia Massive Layoffs Go Viral — TikTok Responds
high.summary: Reports have gone viral that ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok, has laid off approximately 90% of Tokopedia employees, following TikTok's acquisition of a 75% stake in Tokopedia in late 2023. TikTok confirmed it is conducting an organizational restructuring of its R&D division but framed it as a strategic alignment for long-term growth rather than a mass layoff. This development raises significant concerns about the future of one of Indonesia's largest e-commerce platforms and its workforce.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Prepares Tax Incentives for Investors Entering Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII)
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa confirmed the government will provide tax incentives for foreign investors entering the Indonesia International Financial Center (PFII), benchmarked against international standards. The incentive framework will reference global IFC best practices, including Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) in the UAE. This is a significant policy signal for foreign capital attraction and could materially impact Indonesia's competitiveness as a regional financial hub.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya: PFII Funds Can Flow into Danantara Projects and Government Bonds
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa outlined how foreign investor funds channeled through the PFII could be directed toward domestic strategic projects, including those managed by state investment body Danantara (BPI), as well as government bonds (SUN). The minister emphasized participation would be market-based and voluntary, with attractive projects to be offered to foreign investors. This has direct implications for government debt financing and the viability of large-scale infrastructure and investment projects in Indonesia.

high.title: Viral News of Tokopedia Mass Layoffs: TikTok Speaks Up
high.summary: TikTok, the majority shareholder of Tokopedia (holding 75% since late 2023), confirmed it is conducting organizational adjustments to its R&D division amid viral reports of up to 90% employee layoffs at Tokopedia. The company framed the move as aligning its R&D organization toward sustainable long-term growth. This is a significant corporate event affecting one of Indonesia's largest e-commerce platforms and its thousands of employees.

high.title: Indonesian Tourists No Longer Need to Exchange Currency — QRIS Now Accepted in Japan
high.summary: Bank Indonesia officially launched Cross-Border QRIS with Japan, allowing Indonesian tourists to pay directly via QR code without exchanging currency. BI Governor Perry Warjiyo announced the implementation, noting that approximately 500,000 travelers between both countries annually will benefit. This marks a significant step in Indonesia's local currency transaction (LCT) strategy and digital payment expansion.

high.title: Japan's Stock Market Plunges Over 12% — Worse Than the 1987 Black Monday Crisis
high.summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 index crashed 12.4%, falling 4,451 points — the largest single-day point drop in Nikkei history and worse than the 1987 Black Monday crash. Major Japanese conglomerates including Mitsubishi, Mitsui, and Sumitomo each fell more than 14%, with Mitsui losing nearly 20% of its market capitalization. This global market shock poses significant spillover risks for Indonesian equities and investor sentiment.

medium.title: Finance Minister Purbaya on Calls to Abolish JHT Pension Fund Tax: 'In This Economy, Let's Assess First'
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya responded to public pressure to remove the tax on JHT (Old Age Security) pension fund withdrawals, clarifying that 96% of recipients are already exempt as their withdrawals are below IDR 50 million. The government is open to reviewing the tax rate for the remaining 4% but will weigh it against current economic conditions. This signals a potential regulatory change to pension fund taxation that could affect workers and long-term savings incentives.

medium.title: Presidential Special Advisor Discusses PT Granito's Fate, Mentions Danantara Readiness to Take Over
medium.summary: Presidential Special Advisor for Labor Said Iqbal met with Danantara COO Dony Oskaria to discuss measures to prevent mass layoffs (PHK) at PT Granito. It was revealed in a government task force meeting that Danantara is prepared to take over PT Granito if the company cannot survive and continues to lay off employees. This development highlights Danantara's expanding role as a state investment vehicle potentially intervening in distressed companies to protect employment.

medium.title: KAI Reshuffles Board of Directors; Former Pelita Air CEO Appointed as Commercial Director
medium.summary: State-owned railway company PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) restructured its board of directors on June 30, 2026, as approved by its Annual General Shareholders Meeting. The reshuffle includes the dismissal of two directors and a renaming of several key positions, including the creation of a new Commercial Director role filled by the former CEO of Pelita Air. This corporate governance change at a major SOE listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange may impact KAI's strategic direction and business development going forward.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia CEO Daud Joseph Resigns — Company Explains Reasons
medium.summary: PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) announced the resignation of its Director General (CEO) Daud Joseph effective July 2, 2026, citing purely personal reasons. The state-owned company assured stakeholders that operational activities will continue uninterrupted during the leadership transition, which will be conducted in accordance with applicable governance procedures. The sudden departure of top leadership at a major state-owned enterprise warrants monitoring for potential strategic or financial implications.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia Denies Reports of Delayed Salary Payments for 32,000 Employees and Retirees
medium.summary: PT Pos Indonesia refuted circulating reports that salaries for 32,000 employees and retirees were paid late, with Corporate Secretary Iwan Gunawan confirming that July 1 salary disbursements were completed on time. The company also clarified that the CEO's resignation is unrelated to any salary payment issues. The denial comes amid heightened scrutiny of the state-owned postal company following its CEO's sudden departure.

medium.title: Ministry of Cooperatives Partners with Agrinas Palma to Manage Productive Palm Oil Land Through Cooperatives
medium.summary: The Ministry of Cooperatives signed an MoU with PT Agrinas Palma Nusantara to develop a cooperative-based palm oil plantation ecosystem, covering approximately 850,000 hectares of reclaimed forest land with plans to expand to 1.25 million hectares. At least 20% of the area (around 250,000 hectares) is mandated for plasma cooperatives, potentially forming up to 250 cooperatives. This represents a significant restructuring of palm oil land management with implications for the agricultural and cooperative sectors in Indonesia.

medium.title: 30,000 Red-White Village Cooperative Managers to Begin Deployment in August
medium.summary: The Ministry of Cooperatives announced that 30,000 managers for the Koperasi Desa/Kelurahan Merah Putih (Red-White Village Cooperatives) program will be deployed to their home regions in early August 2026 following completion of national defense training under the Ministry of Defense. Managers will be placed in cooperatives alongside the completion of physical warehouse and retail infrastructure construction. This marks a major operational milestone for the government's nationwide grassroots cooperative program aimed at strengthening rural economic activity.

medium.title: KAI Reshuffles Board of Directors: Former Pelita Air CEO Appointed as Commercial Director
medium.summary: State-owned railway company PT Kereta Api Indonesia (KAI) restructured its board of directors effective June 30, 2026, as approved by the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPS). Two directors were dismissed and several directorate titles were renamed, including the creation of a new Commercial Director role filled by the former CEO of Pelita Air. This corporate restructuring is relevant for KAI investors and stakeholders monitoring the company's strategic direction and operational governance.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia Denies Reports of Late Salary Payments to 32,000 Employees and Retirees
medium.summary: PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) officially denied circulating reports that salaries for 32,000 employees and retirees were delayed, with Corporate Secretary Iwan Gunawan confirming payments were made on time on July 1. The company also clarified that the resignation of CEO Daud Joseph was unrelated to any salary payment issues. This matters to investors as it addresses concerns about the financial health of the state-owned enterprise.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia CEO Daud Joseph Resigns, Cites Personal Reasons
medium.summary: Daud Joseph officially resigned as President Director of state-owned PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) effective July 2, 2026, citing purely personal reasons. The company assured stakeholders that operational activities will continue uninterrupted during the leadership transition. As a major state-owned enterprise, the leadership change warrants monitoring for its potential impact on the company's strategic direction and ongoing restructuring efforts.

medium.title: Dozens of Japanese Companies Go Bankrupt Due to Weak Yen
medium.summary: A total of 45 Japanese companies have gone bankrupt in 2026, a 30% increase compared to the previous year, according to Tokyo Shoko Research, marking the highest level since 2022. The bankruptcies are driven by a weakening Yen and rising economic costs, particularly affecting small businesses while exporters benefit. This is relevant for Indonesian investors as Japan is a major trade and investment partner, and Yen volatility can affect bilateral trade and Japanese FDI flows into Indonesia.

medium.title: IDX Adds 2 Stocks Classified as Controlled by a Small Group of Shareholders — Here is the List
medium.summary: Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) has designated two new stocks — PT Habco Trans Maritima Tbk (HATM) and PT Delta Giri Wacana Tbk (DGWG) — under the High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) category, with ownership concentration above 90%. HATM's shares are 96.09% controlled by a small group of parties, while DGWG stands at 97.35%. Investors should exercise caution as HSC-classified stocks carry higher liquidity and manipulation risks.
